content.text:
**Short answer:** *Not obviously.* Gold looks **strategically supported**, but at roughly **$4,300/oz spot** and with **GLD around $396.66** today, it is hard to call it clearly “undervalued” unless you believe one or more of these will happen: real yields fall, the dollar weakens, central-bank buying stays unusually strong, or geopolitical/fiscal risk rises further. ([vantagemarkets.com](https://www.vantagemarkets.com/market-analysis/xauusd-gold-price-analysis-june-8-2026/?utm_source=openai))

### Why gold may still be undervalued

- **Central-bank and Asian investment demand remain strong.** World Gold Council data for Q1 2026 shows continued positive ETF demand, with global gold ETF holdings rising by **62 tonnes** in the quarter, and Asia generating consistent inflows. ([gold.org](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-demand-trends/gold-demand-trends-q1-2026/investment?utm_source=openai))  
- **ETF demand has re-accelerated.** WGC’s June 2026 ETF update says global gold ETF holdings reached **3,932 tonnes**, the highest month-end level on record. That suggests institutional demand has not disappeared despite high prices. ([gold.org](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/etf-flows?page=0&utm_source=openai))  
- **Gold’s “insurance value” may be higher than old models imply.** If investors are increasingly worried about fiscal deficits, currency debasement, geopolitical fragmentation, or reserve diversification away from the dollar, gold can trade above what a simple real-yield model would suggest.

### Why it may not be undervalued

- **Real yields are still high.** The U.S. 10-year TIPS yield was around **2.17% on June 5, 2026**, which is normally a headwind for gold because gold pays no interest. ([tradingeconomics.com](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/10-year-tips-yield?utm_source=openai))  
- **Gold has already repriced a lot.** At around **$4,300/oz**, gold is no longer obviously cheap versus its own history; a lot of the “debasement / central-bank buying / safe-haven” story may already be in the price. ([vantagemarkets.com](https://www.vantagemarkets.com/market-analysis/xauusd-gold-price-analysis-june-8-2026/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Jewelry and price-sensitive physical demand can weaken at high prices.** When gold rises sharply, some traditional demand tends to shift toward profit-taking or lower consumption, even if investment demand remains strong.

### My practical view

I’d frame gold as **fair-to-slightly-expensive on traditional valuation metrics**, but **not necessarily overvalued in a regime-change scenario**.

So:

- If your thesis is **“rates stay high, dollar firm, risk assets stable”** → gold probably does **not** look undervalued.  
- If your thesis is **“real yields fall, dollar weakens, central banks keep buying, fiscal/geopolitical risks remain elevated”** → gold could still be **undervalued** despite the high nominal price.  
- For a portfolio, gold is easier to justify as a **diversifier/insurance asset** than as a screaming bargain.

A reasonable conclusion: **gold is not cheap, but it may still be under-owned relative to the macro risks investors are trying to hedge.**
